messages.content:
Simulate a fictional lost-sales inventory system exactly. There is no stochastic prediction and no missing information beyond the explicit reporting cutoff.
Receipts add quantity to stock. Demands consume min(stock, quantity); any unmet quantity is lost (never backlogged). A stockout means strictly positive unmet demand, not merely ending with zero stock.
For raw report histories: first keep reports with received_time <= knowledge_cutoff. Then choose the highest visible revision for EACH event_id. Revisions REPLACE earlier reports, not add to them. Then keep chosen events with event_time <= target_time. Apply these events in (event_time, event_id) order, starting from initial_stock. Ignore any report not visible at the knowledge cutoff even if its event occurred earlier. Arrival order is not event order.
The canonical arm supplies the already selected eligible events in event-time order. The snapshot arm supplies the exactly replayed historical state. These are explicitly identified, executable preprocessing interventions.
After the historical reconstruction, apply every event in the given future_schedule in (event_time, event_id) order from the reconstructed stock. This is an explicitly known hypothetical scenario, not privileged knowledge about a real future.
Return five integers through submit_answer: stock_at_target; total historical_lost through target_time using visible revisions; stock_at_horizon after the scenario; future_lost for the scenario ONLY; first_future_stockout_time, the earliest future scenario event time with unmet demand, or -1 if no future demand is unmet. Do not count historical stockouts in that last field.

Then keep chosen events with event_time <= target_time (100). Apply these events in (event_time, event_id) order, starting from initial_stock. Ignore any report not visible at the knowledge cutoff even if its event occurred earlier. Arrival order is not event order.

Important: Since each event has a unique event_id and revision number, but there might be multiple revisions for same event_id with different received_time, we need to pick highest revision among those with received_time <= knowledge_cutoff. In this data, all revisions are 1, and each event_id appears only once. So we keep all of them (since received_time <= knowledge_cutoff means all those with received_time <= 100). We must check each eligible event's received_time. All listed have received_time values ranging from 2 up to 99. All <= 100, so they're all visible. So we keep all for selection. There are no later revisions. So we have entire eligible_events set.

Next, we must keep only those chosen events whose event_time <= target_time = 100. So events with event_time > 100 will be excluded from historical reconstruction. So we need to exclude events with event_time > 100 (i.e., 101 and beyond). Looking at eligible_events, we have event_time from 2 up to 99 (maybe there's event at 99?). The last event is at event_time 99 (event_id: E-5cb41e230e27). So all are within target_time=100. So all events are included for historical reconstruction.

Now apply events in (event_time, event_id) order (i.e., sorted by event_time ascending, and then event_id as tie-breaker) starting from initial_stock = 9.

We must track stock changes and record lost-sales: when a demand occurs, we consume min(stock, demand_quantity). Any unmet quantity is lost. A stockout means strictly positive unmet demand, not just ending stock=0. So for each demand, if demand > stock, then lost = demand - stock. Stock becomes 0 after consuming what we have (stock = 0 after). If stock >= demand, no lost; stock reduces by demand.

We must compute total historical lost up to target_time (i.e., 100) using visible revisions. So we need sum of all lost across historical demands. Also record stock_at_target, which is stock after processing all events with event_time <= target_time (including those exactly at time 100?). Since we have no events at time 100 (looking at data; max is 99). So after processing all events up to 99, we have stock_at_target.

We also need to apply future_schedule events (times 101-125) after reconstructing the historical stock state. Then compute stock_at_horizon after all future_schedule events (including those after horizon? horizon_time=130; the latest future event is at time 125, so all included). It says "After the historical reconstruction, apply every event in the given future_schedule in (event_time, event_id) order from the reconstructed stock. This is an explicitly known hypothetical scenario." The horizon_time is 130; we need stock at horizon after scenario, i.e., after processing all future_schedule events up to horizon_time (including events up to 125). So we compute stock_at_horizon accordingly.

We also need future_lost: total lost sales from future schedule only (i.e., lost from demands that happened in the future schedule). Also need first_future_stockout_time: the earliest future scenario event time where there was unmet demand (i.e., where lost > 0). If none, then -1. Note that we only count stockouts for future events, exclude historical stockouts.

We must return these five ints via submit_answer.
